g.data-info: Parenchyma between the xylem and phloem groups; a pith is small or absent.
Four arms of vessels; small protoxylem lies at the outside and large metaxylem meets at the centre.
Patches of sieve tubes lying between the xylem arms, so the bundle is radial.
One layer of thin-walled cells inside the endodermis; lateral roots arise here.
Innermost cortex layer whose cell walls carry the Casparian strip.
A band of waterproof suberin in the radial walls of endodermal cells that forces water to pass through the cells.
Many layers of loosely packed parenchyma that store food and pass water inward.
Outermost single layer of the root, without a cuticle, that absorbs water.
Tubular outgrowths of epiblema cells that greatly increase the surface for absorbing water.
